sections.label: Ministerial Statements Sitting Order
sections.summary: Ministerial Statements on the Leader of the Opposition and the Middle East should be taken before the debate on the Address of Thanks.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: First, my Ministerial Statement on "Duties and Privileges of the Leader of the Opposition" sets out the Leader of the Opposition's duties and privileges for this term of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It would thus be apposite for my Ministerial Statement to be taken before the rest of the proceedings at this Sitting, including the debate on the Address of Thanks.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: I am also moving that my Ministerial Statement be taken before the business Motion on Speech Time, standing in my name as the two are closely related.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Second, the two Ministerial Statements on "Situation in the Middle East" and the Ministerial Statement on "Singaporeans' Response to Situation in the Middle East" are of current public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Also, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan is due to deliver Singapore's statement at the 80th United Nations General Assembly and leaves for that tonight.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It would be good for Singaporeans to hear the Government's position on this before he leaves.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It would thus be best for these Ministerial Statements to be taken before the debate on the Address of Thanks.
